threads.thread_goal: Align on final tier structure, benefits, and pricing before documentation freeze.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the initial tier structure for A1 and would like to get feedback before we lock it in. We're proposing three tiers: Basic, Premium, and Elite. Each tier has distinct benefits and pricing aligned to our key customer segments. The draft is ready for review—please share thoughts on the naming, benefit mix, and pricing bands. We need to finalize this by EOD tomorrow to stay on track with T1.

Thanks for getting this started. I've reviewed the draft and the three-tier approach makes sense from a sales perspective. The naming is clear and easy to communicate. One question: are the pricing bands aligned with what finance has validated for margin impact? I want to make sure we're not overselling benefits that will erode margins. Also, the Elite tier benefits look comprehensive—have we modeled the usage scenarios to confirm they're sustainable?

I think the structure is reasonable. The three tiers seem appropriate. I'll need to review the margin calculations more carefully, but the general approach aligns with what we discussed. One thing I'm not entirely clear on—how do the eligibility rules work for each tier? We should make sure the rules are straightforward so the sales team doesn't get confused when positioning them.

Good point on eligibility. I've documented the rules in A1—they're based on customer tenure, annual spend, and segment classification. The rules are designed to be simple enough for sales to apply without constant back-and-forth. I'll add a quick reference table to make it even clearer. Regarding margin validation, I've worked with finance on the benefit costs, but I want to confirm the pricing bands one more time. Should we schedule a quick sync with finance to lock this in?

Yes, a sync with finance would be helpful. I want to make sure the incentive structure I'm designing in T2 aligns with the pricing. If the margins are tighter than expected, we may need to adjust how we position certain benefits or reconsider the tier boundaries. Once we have finance sign-off on the pricing, I can finalize the sales pitch framework in A2.

I've been looking at the tier structure from an operations perspective, and I think we need to be careful about the upgrade/downgrade paths. The Basic to Premium transition looks straightforward, but the Premium to Elite jump might create friction if customers don't see clear value. Have we thought about how we'll handle members who want to move between tiers mid-cycle? This will affect the playbook we're building in T3.

That's a solid observation. The upgrade/downgrade logic is part of the operations playbook in A3, which I'm working on in parallel with T1. I'll make sure the tier transition rules are clear and that we have a simple process for mid-cycle changes. The key is to keep it operationally feasible without creating too many exceptions. I'll incorporate this into the playbook and share it with you for feedback.

I think we should move forward with the three-tier structure. The naming and general benefit mix seem solid. We'll need to confirm the pricing with finance, but I don't see a major blocker. Let's get that finance sync scheduled and then we can finalize A1. Once that's locked, we can move on to the sales pitch and training materials.

Agreed. I'll set up the finance sync for tomorrow morning. Once we have pricing locked, I can move quickly on the sales pitch framework in A2 and the training outline in T5. The sooner we have those ready, the sooner we can get the teams aligned. I'll also start drafting the objection-handling guide so we're ready to brief the sales team.

Perfect. I'll finalize the eligibility rules and add the reference table to A1 by EOD today. Once finance confirms the pricing, we'll have D1 and D2 locked. Then we can move to the next phase with confidence. Thanks for the thorough review, everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Lock sales pitch, objection handling, and training approach for launch.

messages.text: I've drafted the sales pitch framework for A2 and a preliminary training outline. The pitch is structured around the value proposition for each tier, with clear talking points for positioning. I've also started on the top objections and recommended responses. The training outline in T5 covers product knowledge, pitch practice, and Q&A. Please review and let me know if the approach aligns with what you're expecting.

Thanks for getting this drafted. The pitch framework looks solid and the structure is easy to follow. I have a few questions on the objection handling—specifically around the 'cost vs. value' objection for the Premium tier. How are you recommending the team respond when a customer pushes back on price? Also, do we need to include any compliance or data protection messaging in the pitch, or should that be handled separately?

Good questions. For the cost objection, I've recommended focusing on the ROI and the specific benefits that justify the price point. The idea is to help the sales team reframe the conversation around value rather than just cost. As for compliance messaging, I think that should be a separate section in the pitch guide—maybe a quick reference on data handling and consent. I can add that to A2. Do you want me to coordinate with the legal or compliance team on the exact wording?

The pitch framework seems reasonable. I think the training outline is good too. One thing I want to make sure of—are we planning mandatory training for all sales staff, or is it optional? We need to be clear on expectations so everyone is prepared before launch. Also, how long is the training session? We need to make sure it fits into the team's schedule without disrupting daily operations.

I'm proposing mandatory training for all sales staff who will be selling the new tiers. The session is designed to be 90 minutes—product overview, pitch practice, and Q&A. I'm planning to run multiple sessions so teams can attend without disrupting their schedules. I'll coordinate with team leads to find the best times. The training materials will be available in A5 for reference after the session. Does that approach work for you?

The 90-minute format sounds reasonable. I'd suggest we also prepare a quick reference guide that sales can keep at their desk—something they can pull up quickly if they need to check a talking point or objection response. That would complement the training and help with consistency. I can work with you on that once A2 is finalized.

From the membership operations side, I want to make sure the training also covers what happens after the sale—how to onboard the member into their tier, what systems they need to access, and how to handle any issues that come up. The pitch is important, but the follow-through is critical. Should we include a section in T5 on post-sale operations?

That's a great point. I'll add a section to the training on post-sale handoff and onboarding. The membership team will need to be trained on the same material so they understand the tier structure and can support the sales team. I'll coordinate with you on the membership team training schedule. We should probably run that in parallel with the sales training.

Okay, so we're looking at mandatory training for both sales and membership teams, 90 minutes each, with multiple sessions to accommodate schedules. That works. I think we should also have a brief refresher session a week after launch in case there are questions that come up during the first few days. Let's lock in the training dates and get them on the calendar.

I'll finalize A2 with the compliance section and the post-sale operations content by tomorrow. Then I'll coordinate with team leads to schedule the training sessions. I'll aim to have all sessions scheduled by end of week. The refresher session is a good idea—I'll add that to the plan. Once we have the training dates locked, I'll update A5 with the full schedule.

Perfect. Once A2 is finalized and the training schedule is locked, we'll have D3 and D4 confirmed. That will clear the path for the membership team to prepare their materials and for the customer service team to get ready with the FAQ. I'll start working on A8 in parallel so we're ready for the next phase.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on data fields, tagging rules, and pre-launch data clean-up scope.

messages.text: I've completed the initial data audit for T8 and drafted the data fields matrix for A4. The audit shows that our current membership database has some gaps in key fields like tier eligibility indicators and segment classifications. I've identified the required fields for the new tier structure and documented the tagging rules. The clean-up scope is significant but manageable if we prioritize. Please review A4 and let me know if there are fields we're missing or if the tagging rules need adjustment.

Thanks for the audit. I've reviewed A4 and the fields look comprehensive. From a sales perspective, I need to make sure we have clear segment classification fields so we can target the right tiers to the right customers. The tagging rules seem solid, but I have a question—how are we handling customers who don't fit neatly into one segment? Do we have a default tier assignment, or do we need to manually review those cases?

Good question. For customers who don't fit neatly into a segment, I've proposed a default assignment to the Basic tier with a flag for manual review. That way, we don't lose anyone, but we also flag cases that need attention. The sales team can then reach out to those customers and determine the right tier placement. I'll add that logic to the tagging rules in A4.

I've been looking at the data clean-up scope from T8, and I'm concerned about the timeline. The audit shows we need to clean up about 15% of the customer records to meet the minimum data standards. That's a lot of manual work. Do we have the resources to complete this before launch, or do we need to prioritize which segments get cleaned up first?

That's a valid concern. I've prioritized the clean-up by segment—we'll focus on the high-value segments first since those are the ones we're targeting for the new tiers. The lower-priority segments can be cleaned up post-launch if needed. I've documented the priority clean-up actions in T8. We should confirm which actions are in-scope for the pre-launch phase and which can be deferred.

I think we should focus on the high-value segments for the pre-launch clean-up. That makes sense from a business perspective. We can address the lower-priority segments after launch. Let's confirm the final set of required fields in A4 and lock in the clean-up scope for D5 and D6. Once that's done, we can move forward with the data preparation.

Agreed. I want to make sure the segment classification is accurate so we can target the right tiers. Once the data is cleaned up, I'll need a clean export of the customer list with tier assignments so I can use it for the launch campaign planning. That will help me understand the size of each tier segment and plan the messaging accordingly.

I'll make sure to provide that export once the data clean-up is complete. I'll also include a data quality report so you can see what was cleaned and any remaining issues. That should give you everything you need for the launch campaign. Let me finalize A4 with the confirmed fields and tagging rules, and we can lock in D5 and D6.

threads.thread_goal: Define pilot scope, success criteria, and adjustments before full rollout.

messages.text: I've drafted the pilot plan for T10. I'm proposing a pilot cohort of 500 customers from our high-value segment, running for 2 weeks. The pilot will test the tier structure, onboarding process, and member experience. We'll collect feedback through surveys and support tickets to identify any issues before full launch. The success criteria are: 80% of pilot members successfully onboarded, zero critical issues, and positive feedback on tier clarity. Please review and let me know if the scope and timeline work for you.

The pilot scope looks reasonable. 500 customers from the high-value segment is a good size—large enough to surface issues but small enough to manage. The 2-week timeline is tight, but doable. I have a question on the feedback collection—are we planning to reach out to pilot members directly, or are we relying on support tickets and surveys? I want to make sure we capture feedback from members who might not proactively report issues.

Good point. I'm planning to send a brief survey to all pilot members at the end of the first week and again at the end of the pilot. That way, we'll get proactive feedback rather than just relying on support tickets. I'll also have the customer service team flag any issues that come up during the pilot so we can address them quickly. The survey will focus on tier clarity, benefit understanding, and overall satisfaction.

I want to make sure the pilot also tests the operations playbook in A3. We need to see if the onboarding process, tier transitions, and support workflows actually work as documented. I'd suggest we have the membership team actively monitor the pilot and note any process issues or bottlenecks. That will help us refine A3 before full launch.

Absolutely. The pilot is as much about testing the operations as it is about testing the tier structure. I'll make sure the membership team is actively involved in monitoring the pilot and documenting any issues with the playbook. We'll use that feedback to refine A3 before full launch. I'll also track the time it takes to complete each process step so we can identify any bottlenecks.

The pilot plan sounds solid. I think 500 customers and 2 weeks is a good scope. Let's confirm the pilot cohort selection criteria and the feedback collection method. Once we have D7 locked, we can move forward with setting up the pilot. I want to make sure we're ready to launch the full program within the 21-day window, so the pilot needs to be tight and efficient.

I agree. The timeline is tight, but the pilot plan is realistic. Once we have the pilot results, we'll need to move quickly on any adjustments. I'm assuming we'll have a debrief session after the pilot to review the findings and decide what changes need to be made before full launch. That's where D8 comes in—we need to agree on which changes are critical and which can be deferred.

Yes, I'll schedule a debrief session for the day after the pilot ends. I'll prepare a summary report in A7 with the pilot results, key findings, and recommended adjustments. We'll review that together and decide what needs to be changed before full launch. I'm confident the pilot will surface any major issues so we can address them before we go live with the full program.

Okay, let's lock in the pilot scope and timeline. I'm approving the 500-customer cohort, 2-week duration, and the feedback collection approach. That's D7 confirmed. Once the pilot is complete and we have the results in A7, we'll review and make any necessary adjustments before full launch. Let's move forward with setting up the pilot.

next_steps.when: debrief and A7 report after pilot

threads.thread_goal: Finalize cross-team launch timeline, KPIs, and review cadence.

messages.text: I've drafted an integrated timeline for T11 that maps out all the key milestones from design through full launch. The timeline includes design phase (days 1-7), training phase (days 8-12), pilot phase (days 13-15), and full launch (day 16). I've also identified the dependencies between sales and membership tasks so we can coordinate effectively. Please review the timeline and let me know if the milestones and dependencies are accurate.

I've reviewed the timeline and it looks solid. The phasing makes sense and the dependencies are clear. One thing I want to confirm—the training phase is scheduled for days 8-12, but we need to make sure the sales pitch and training materials are finalized by day 7. That's a tight deadline for A2 and T5. I can make it happen, but I want to flag that as a critical path item.

Understood. A2 and T5 are on the critical path. I'll make sure to prioritize those deliverables and provide you with any feedback you need by day 6 so you have time to finalize. The timeline assumes we have D1, D2, D3, and D4 locked by day 5, which should give us enough time to prepare the training materials.

The timeline is reasonable. I want to make sure we have a clear handoff between the design phase and the training phase. Once the tier structure and pitch are finalized, we need to make sure the membership team is ready to support the sales team during training. I also want to confirm the post-launch review cadence. How often are we planning to review performance after launch?

Good question. I've drafted a post-launch review plan in T12 that includes weekly performance reviews for the first 8 weeks. The reviews will cover KPIs like tier adoption, member satisfaction, and sales performance. I'm proposing a weekly cadence for the first month, then bi-weekly for weeks 5-8. That should give us enough visibility to catch any issues early without creating too much overhead.

I want to make sure the post-launch reviews include operational metrics, not just sales metrics. We need to track things like onboarding time, support ticket volume, and member satisfaction with the tier experience. That will help us identify any operational issues that might be impacting the overall success of the program.

Absolutely. I'll make sure T12 includes operational KPIs alongside the sales metrics. The weekly reviews will cover tier adoption, member satisfaction, support metrics, and any issues that come up. I'll coordinate with you on the operational metrics so we're tracking the right things.

Perfect. So we have the integrated timeline in T11 with clear milestones and dependencies, and the post-launch review cadence in T12 with both sales and operational metrics. I'll finalize A5 with the complete launch communication and training plan, including the timeline and review schedule. Once that's done, we'll have everything we need for the readiness checklist in A6.

Good. Let's finalize the timeline and review cadence. I want to make sure we have a clear readiness checklist in A6 that covers all the critical items before launch. Once we have that locked, we can move into execution mode. The timeline is tight, but I think we can make it work if we stay focused on the critical path items.
